title: Give a new visitor a useful first action beyond authentication
type: Observed usability issue
confidence: High: live anonymous production browser
problem: The first screen is largely a large logo plus Login, Register and Forgot Password. The anonymous navigation exposes Home and F.A.Q, without an obvious league, scores, standings or check-in entry. There is no explanatory heading describing what a new visitor can do.
impact: A new player needs prior instructions or assumes every task requires account creation. Friends checking results cannot discover the relevant public route from this landing page.
recommendation: Retain the logo and add a short purpose statement and permission-appropriate task links: Find a league, Scores & standings, and Sign in to my account. Keep management private. Decide with the owner which already-public views should be discoverable rather than widening access automatically.
complexity: Small–medium: content and navigation; no scoring rewrite
risk: Medium: public/private destinations and deep links must retain existing authorization
acceptance: A first-time visitor can identify the site purpose and find an intended public result view without being told a URL.

title: Bound player-search suggestions and keep Create/Close reachable
type: UI interaction defect reproduced with synthetic display data
confidence: High for this 16-result fixture; real account creation not performed
problem: At 375px, the suggestions overlap the action area; a normal Create New Player click was intercepted by a player suggestion. Names truncate to nearly identical Sample Play… labels. Clearing the query returns all players again, so that is not a reliable dismissal mechanism. A no-match query made Create reachable.
impact: A newcomer can select the wrong person, fail to find the create action, or abandon claiming. The workaround is not discoverable.
recommendation: Use a bounded listbox/autocomplete with wrapped names, a clear dismissal path and a separate persistent Create New Player action. Show only existing non-sensitive context needed to distinguish matches. Preserve exact ownership/duplicate-claim checks and explicit confirmation.
risk: Medium: selection/automatic-claim state and duplicate rejection must be regression-tested
acceptance: With at least 16 matches at 375px, all results remain distinguishable and Create/Close work without clearing or inventing a query.

title: Make mobile score entry fit and pair opponents by game
type: Observed layout defect plus design recommendation
confidence: High for geometry; saving was not attempted
problem: The 375px layout has a 425px document width. Tabs and fields are clipped sideways; two opponent cards become vertically separated. Even the default three games require comparing scores across separated sections, with the save action below the first viewport.
impact: Courtside entry requires scrolling and remembering which opponent/game is being edited; accidental transposition is more likely.
recommendation: Preserve the useful two-team comparison on desktop. On phones, show one match card with Game 1/2/3 rows and adjacent scores for both teams, an explicit date, and a readable review/save action. Remove page-level overflow; do not change scoring rules or payloads.
risk: Medium–high: game indexing, paired score submission, date and standings updates must remain unchanged
acceptance: At 375px and 390px there is no page-wide horizontal scroll, and each pair of game scores can be entered together.

title: Separate the basic scramble task from advanced configuration
type: Observed layout/usability issue
confidence: High for rendered controls; full setup completion not timed
problem: The mobile Scrambler reaches 433px document width at a 375px viewport. Max Team Size, Number of Teams, random/lock options and advanced top-player controls occupy the top; major buttons clip, and management/retrieval tools continue down a long page.
impact: The league-night operator must scan many expert options before taking the common action, with uncertainty about which team-count control is active.
recommendation: Offer a basic sequence: league/session → signed-in players → team size or number of teams → preview. Put advanced balancing and top-player settings in a clearly labelled expandable section, preserving every existing option and an expert view.
risk: High if selection/balancing state is changed; begin with layout/disclosure only
acceptance: The normal preview path is visible and readable on a phone without exposing every advanced option or losing the existing algorithm.

title: Restore navigation and league context when a session page is refreshed
type: Source-supported functional risk, not a real-session authentication test
confidence: Medium–high: fixture browser plus source; needs owner confirmation with an actual session
problem: Direct-entry fixture pages can show Player/Manager component content while the navbar still shows only Home/F.A.Q and lacks league selection. AuthService starts its BehaviorSubject at false, AppComponent does not hydrate it, and NavMenu depends on it. League selection is also an in-memory BehaviorSubject. The paired screenshot shows the expected post-login layout after deliberately modelling that client state.
impact: A returning player may appear logged out or lose the working league after refresh, despite an otherwise valid server session; some direct views are blank or ambiguous.
recommendation: Verify this exact real-session refresh case first. If confirmed, initialize the navigation from existing read-only session endpoints and restore/validate a selected league. This is UI-state restoration, not a new cookie, role, password or authentication system.
risk: Medium–high: preserve ordinary/legacy distinctions and reject stale or unassigned league selections
acceptance: An actually authenticated user can refresh a permitted deep link and retain correct navigation/context without changing authentication behavior.

title: Keep mobile standings readable and keyboard-scrollable
type: Observed usability/accessibility issue
confidence: High for synthetic populated tables and axe result
problem: The outer page fits, but standings columns continue inside a narrow horizontal region; total points/wins disappear to the right. Nested Overall/Division and Men/Women tabs compete for width. Axe flags scrollable-region-focusable on some table states.
impact: A phone user cannot easily compare rank, name and useful totals together; keyboard users may struggle to reach the horizontal region.
recommendation: Keep desktop/print tables. Use a concise mobile summary with rank/name/essential total visible, optional detail expansion and clear scroll affordance. Where full tables remain, make the labelled scroll container keyboard-operable and consider a pinned identifier column.
risk: Medium: preserve sort order, round/matchup meaning, divisions, adjustments and printed output
acceptance: A user can read their rank and essential total without sideways hunting, and can keyboard-scroll any remaining full table.

title: Use the existing accessible dialog pattern for the custom claim overlay
type: Observed accessibility defect in a display-only form
confidence: High: keyboard and DOM inspection
problem: The custom overlay has no dialog role. During 24 Tab steps, five focus stops were outside it, including background actions. Axe also reports mat-option required-parent issues. This is not equivalent to the application’s existing Material confirmation-dialog pattern.
impact: Keyboard/screen-reader users can lose context or operate background controls while the overlay is visually active.
recommendation: Reuse an appropriate existing Material dialog/listbox pattern, give the dialog a name, move focus inside it, constrain focus while open, and restore focus on close. Retain explicit claim confirmation and the current backend ownership validation.
risk: Medium: cancellation, search selection and automatic claiming must continue correctly
acceptance: Tab stays within the active dialog, Escape/Cancel works predictably, the title is announced, and focus returns to the trigger.

title: Move league setup out of the Scrambler’s nested tool tabs
type: Observed information-architecture issue
confidence: High for location and layout; no creation/settings save tested
problem: Add League/Add Division are nested below the scramble configuration in management tabs. At 375px those pages are approximately 2076–2335px tall, with tab pagination adding navigation friction. An Add Player tab could not be directly tapped without navigating pagination.
impact: Occasional managers struggle to discover setup tools, and routine setup requires unrelated scrolling through play controls.
recommendation: Provide a permission-appropriate Manage League entry with Players, Divisions and Settings. Keep existing routes/actions available initially; do not rewrite ownership or the shared-password unlock workflow.
risk: Medium: existing league ownership, Manager scope and unlocked administration must remain intact
acceptance: An authorized manager can discover league setup without passing through scramble controls.

title: Make login behave like a standard keyboard-friendly form
type: Observed local UI behavior, no login sent
confidence: High for frontend observation
problem: With a syntactically valid synthetic email and blank password, Submit remains enabled. Enter from the password field did not submit. Source uses click-driven login fields rather than a form submit handler. Registration provides some inline feedback but differs from login.
impact: Keyboard users hit a dead end with Enter, and users receive avoidable submit-time errors instead of clear required-field feedback.
recommendation: Use a semantic form/submit interaction, keep server validation, and present accessible required-field and format feedback. Add suitable email/inputmode and autocomplete hints. Do not change credential requirements or expose account existence.
risk: Low–medium: preserve current account-neutral errors, throttling and security checks
acceptance: Enter submits valid local form input; missing required values are explained clearly, and autofill/password managers receive appropriate hints.

title: Raise text contrast without changing the brand palette
type: Automated accessibility finding with visual confirmation
confidence: High for sampled states; not a complete compliance assessment
problem: Axe measured enabled production navbar text at 4.22:1 (#9a9da0 on #343a40) and some normal-size tab text at 4.29:1 (#7a7a7a on white), below 4.5:1. Some helper text also needs review. Disabled controls and logo text have different exceptions and are not blanket failures.
impact: Reduced readability outdoors and for people with low vision; subtle selected/unselected states become harder to see.
recommendation: Adjust a small shared set of foreground/background tokens and selected/focus styles. Preserve navy/blue identity and strong Gold/Silver grouping; validate actual text sizes and states rather than replacing the palette.
risk: Low, provided disabled/selected/focus distinctions are retained
acceptance: Sampled enabled text meets its applicable contrast threshold, including focus/selected states, without relying on color alone.

title: Make failure feedback actionable and avoid blocking the next step
type: Observed simulated-error rendering plus source review
confidence: High for displayed message; server failure not caused or tested
problem: A deliberately aborted local request produces a generic Login Failed notice. Source uses the same generic copy for most non-429 failures, and error snackbars omit a duration. A persistent overlay can obstruct controls unless explicitly closed.
impact: Users cannot distinguish a connection problem from bad input and may repeatedly retry. The message competes with the form instead of guiding recovery.
recommendation: Keep account-neutral wording but distinguish retryable connection failures from input problems; anchor errors to the task, announce them accessibly and keep controls reachable. For saved data, show an explicit success state and what was saved rather than implying a failed operation succeeded.
risk: Medium: avoid leaking backend/SQL/account details or altering retry semantics
acceptance: A user can identify the next safe action, dismiss the message by keyboard, and continue without covered controls.

title: Explain empty, unselected and unavailable states separately
screen: Standings, schedules, teams and profile statistics
type: Observed display-fixture state plus design recommendation
confidence: Medium: data availability and real permissions were not exercised
problem: Some direct-entry views show empty tables or a selector with little explanation. The user cannot tell whether no league is selected, no results exist, a filter is empty, or data failed. Zero profile statistics in these fixtures must not be interpreted as a production defect.
impact: New and returning users can mistake missing context for missing records or a broken site.
recommendation: Provide distinct states with a contextual next action: Choose a league, No rounds recorded yet, No results match this filter, or Could not load—retry. Keep authorized creation actions separate from public viewing.
risk: Low–medium: distinguish errors from genuine zero values and respect permissions
acceptance: Each empty state explains its cause and a safe next action without misleadingly promising data.

title: Name navigation by user tasks and define league-specific terms
screen: Manager navigation, player statistics and scramble options
type: Usability recommendation grounded in rendered labels
confidence: High for labels; preference/owner decisions remain
problem: Team Management is both a top-level destination and an inner tab; League Teams also exists elsewhere. K/Q, Low Player, Bye, Sub Score and Round versus Matchup assume prior league knowledge.
impact: Experienced operators can learn it, but a new manager has to guess where scores or settings live and what options mean.
recommendation: Keep expert terminology where useful and add concise explanations. Prefer task labels such as Enter Scores and View Standings, with predictable destinations and a short K/Q glossary. Do not rename scoring concepts without owner confirmation.
risk: Medium: terminology changes can confuse existing users; retain familiar names or transitional labels
acceptance: A new manager can locate score entry and distinguish round/matchup standings without external coaching.

title: Explain adjusted and dropped scores at the value, not only in the legend
type: Design opportunity, not a proven color-only WCAG failure
confidence: Medium: rendered fixture and source labels
problem: Dropped/reduced/substitute score conventions require referring back to a compact legend and understanding the calculation. Dense mobile cells hide much of that context.
impact: A player can distrust the total or ask administrators to explain a correct result.
recommendation: Provide an accessible score explanation or expanded row showing raw score, substitute reduction and dropped status in words. Keep all existing calculations, division codes and sort order; retain compact expert/print views.
risk: High if calculation logic is touched; keep this a presentation-only change
acceptance: A player can explain their displayed total using the UI, without changing any verified arithmetic.

title: Reduce repeated entry and uncertainty across registration and claiming
type: Workflow opportunity requiring post-registration confirmation
confidence: Medium: forms inspected separately; no account created in this audit
problem: The journey spans registration, matching/general pickers, optional new-player entry and confirmation. Both registration and player creation ask for first/last names; the audit did not execute registration and cannot assert whether every post-registration path currently prefills them.
impact: Users may not understand the difference between a login account and a league player record, or may create a duplicate profile.
recommendation: Explain the distinction in one sentence and show progress: Account → Find your player → Ready. Reuse supplied names where safe and confirmed, prioritise an existing match, and preserve explicit ownership confirmation.
risk: Medium–high: auto-claim and duplicate protection must stay unchanged
acceptance: The actual registered-user journey avoids unnecessary name re-entry and clearly explains choosing versus creating a player.

title: Use enduring field labels and intention-specific actions
type: Usability recommendation plus partial accessibility findings
confidence: Medium–high
problem: Several actions use generic Submit and some fields lean on placeholder-only naming. Axe also flags an unlabeled text input in the generated scramble preview. Native form buttons are smaller than comfortable courtside controls, while Material controls use a different scale. Tiny hidden Material native inputs are not the actual touch targets and were excluded from violation claims.
impact: Users have to infer what data will be saved, and labels can be lost as values are entered.
recommendation: Use visible persistent labels and verbs such as Save scores, Add player to this team, Create league. Aim for comfortable ~44px targets where feasible, while recognising WCAG AA’s 24px/spacing rules and exceptions.
risk: Low if event handling and submitted fields remain unchanged
acceptance: Each action states its effect and visible labels remain understandable after values are entered.

title: Add a semantic page structure and meaningful image alternatives
type: Accessibility findings; some rules are best-practice checks
confidence: High for sampled pages
problem: The live homepage logo has no alternative text. Many scanned pages lack a main landmark and level-one page heading; profile headings also raise order warnings. Lack of a specific h1 is not by itself a blanket WCAG failure, but the navigation structure is weak.
impact: Assistive-technology users have less context and fewer efficient ways to move to the task.
recommendation: Give the logo a suitable alternative, provide one meaningful page title and main region, a skip link and a sensible heading hierarchy. Use the existing semantic controls/dialog patterns where they already work.
risk: Low: ensure headings do not unintentionally change CSS layout
acceptance: Keyboard/screen-reader users can identify the site/page and jump to main content; decorative images are distinguished correctly.

title: Consolidate visual tokens instead of replacing the visual identity
type: Subjective design preference supported by inconsistency
confidence: Design judgement, not a functional defect
problem: Native grey buttons, blue Material actions, pink accent buttons, large grey panels and differing card/field spacing make related actions look unrelated. This does not mean the working interface needs a fashionable replacement.
impact: A small polish cost is paid on every screen as users relearn action emphasis.
recommendation: Keep the volleyball identity, navy/blue, strong division grouping and useful desktop tables. Define a small spacing/type/action system and apply it incrementally to the highest-use screens first.
complexity: Small initially; medium across the site
risk: Low–medium: global CSS changes can affect many existing templates
acceptance: The same action importance has consistent styling without removing useful expert controls.

title: Keep browser/page identity consistent with League Hub
type: Observed production naming difference; repository title already changed
confidence: High for captured production document.title
problem: The captured production document title still says Allport’s League Scrambler while the displayed logo says League Hub. The source title was already changed before this audit; this is a deployment-state note, not a request to redo that work.
impact: Bookmarks/tabs and subpages provide inconsistent orientation.
recommendation: Include the approved title change in a later separately authorised release and consider a small consistent site identity on interior screens. Do not deploy as part of this audit.
risk: Low
acceptance: Tab/page branding agrees after an authorised release; no authentication or routing change is needed.

title: Keep loading feedback proportional and describe its scope
type: Source-based recommendation; transient screenshot capture limited
confidence: Low–medium; no production performance claim
problem: Source includes a fixed 400px loading wrapper and a 200px spinner. The audit’s delayed-fixture attempt did not reliably capture that transient state, so a mobile overflow or real loading-time failure is not claimed from it.
impact: Large or undifferentiated loading overlays can hide context and leave users unsure which task is waiting.
recommendation: Review the actual loading state with a controlled delay later: concise labelled status near the affected area, accessible busy/live status, preserved page context, and a retry state for failure.
risk: Low–medium: avoid enabling duplicate saves while requests are pending
acceptance: A controlled slow-read check communicates what is loading and recovers accessibly; no real latency target is invented.
